reasoning: The transition engine is being implemented right now, and this message changes what that work must produce: static transitions are ruled out, so the remainder has to be replanned and whatever static path is already in the code comes out. That is a correction — it changes the constraints of work in flight, so it attaches to the checkpoint that work already has and is written in with an update to its decision sheet, never a second row beside it and never a fresh new. It is not a halt: nothing stops, the work keeps running toward the same goal with a narrower constraint. It is not a decision either: a decision settles an open choice inside work that goes on as planned, while this forces the plan for what is left to be rewritten. Being a correction, replanning takes on nothing that did not already exist — the board gains no row and the turn produces zero new pieces of work, however much thought rewriting the sheet costs. The single clause is the correction's own goal in other words, so it carries no second act; naming the repair separately would reopen as fresh work the very thing the correction just changed. Dimensions are named here only because a correction is the stated exception: saying what the running work now touches is the whole point of it. If the boundary of 'static' is not already settled in this project's own vocabulary, that gets one short question in his terms before the replan, rather than a guess.
